title: Gate stall watchdog kills a cold debug build during long links (v0.27.0 cut gate)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
The v0.27.0 cut gate (cut.yml, stage gate, 2026-11-26 00:17Z) stopped at step [01] "debug build (--no-run)" after 22.2 min. No test ran and none failed (summary: "0 failed, 1 stalled").

What happened: the step compiled until about 00:25Z. Then three `rust-lld` links ran at the same time (the `camcraft-ui` test binaries, cold build, `-j 4`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`). The links wrote no output for 15 min. The stall watchdog (`xtask/src/watchdog.rs`, default 15 min for a debug step, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN` not set) then killed the process tree. The tag stage was skipped.

Why it is a bug: a `--no-run` build step is a build, not a test. A cold link of a large test binary can be silent for longer than a test step. The watchdog cannot tell a slow link from a hang, so a cut on a cold runner can fail with no code fault.

Possible fixes (choose one):
1. Give build steps (`--no-run`) the longer limit that `--release` and `--ignored` steps already get (4x).
2. Count child-process CPU time (rustc, rust-lld, cc) as progress, and stall only when the tree is idle.
3. Set `CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN` for the gate step in `cut.yml` (a workaround, not a fix).

Workaround for the current cut: re-run the gate with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN=45` in the cut runner's environment.

Related: #3493 (how the watchdog kills a step; this issue is about when).

Done means: a cold release-tier gate on the cut runner passes step [01] without a stall, and a unit test in `xtask` pins the build-step limit.
